item.title: How Vietnam’s ‘streamlining revolution’ may lead to uneven success
item.description: Third plenums are ordinarily the quiet part of Vietnam’s political calendar. Between its five-yearly congresses, the Communist Party of Vietnam governs through numbered plenums of its Central Committee (CC): the first two settle personnel decisions, and the third, six months on, usually does no more than ratify the term’s work programme. In a statement, Paramount said it has now won approval from regulators representing 68 countries, including the European Union, China, Canada, Brazil and […] Fuente: Variety.

item.title: Chinese drone maker DJI gets another shot at Pentagon blacklist removal
item.description: A US appeal court on Friday gave Chinese drone maker DJI another chance to challenge its inclusion on a Pentagon blacklist of companies allegedly linked to the Chinese military. DJI, a Shenzhen-based drone maker, has been engaged in a years-long legal battle with the US Department of Defence to be removed from the list. The latest ruling from the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit did not remove DJI from the list, but sent the case back to the lower court to reconsider one... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Guangzhou crucibles provide earliest direct evidence of brass-making in East Asia
item.description: For centuries, scholars have read ancient documents describing the production of brass in 10th-century A.D. China. The problem was that the earliest physical evidence of brass production would be found nearly 600 years later, in the 16th century A.D. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Iran war: Trump dismisses concerns over conditions on USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier
item.description: President Donald Trump dismissed concerns on Friday over living conditions and the mental health of service members on a US aircraft carrier deployed against Iran, while confirming the ship would soon rotate out. Asked by reporters whether family members were worried about the situation on the USS Abraham Lincoln, Trump said “no, they’re not”. Trump also rejected the idea that the ship – now in its ninth month at sea – had been deployed for too long. “No, no, no, not nearly enough,” he said. The... item.title: A Welsh family lost Menna Owen at 18 after a cardiac arrest; her heart and lungs were...
item.description: In recent times, there has been a notable drop in family consent rates for organ donation in the UK, resulting in an unprecedented number of patients on transplant waiting lists. To combat this issue, NHS Blood and Transplant has initiated a campaign aimed at boosting registration among potential donors. Menna Owen's experience serves as a poignant reminder that having clear donation preferences can provide solace and ultimately save lives. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Europe is racing to eradicate a crayfish that can reproduce without mating; in the Czech Republic...
item.description: European conservationists are launching a campaign to eradicate new populations of marbled crayfish, notorious for their rapid reproduction and the deadly diseases they carry. Funded by the European Union, these swift action initiatives aim to tackle invasive species promptly, mitigating the risk of extensive environmental and economic harm while safeguarding native ecosystems from foreign invaders. item.title: Men attack trans women in Indonesia after presidential policy deems them a 'threat'
item.description: A series of attacks perpetrated by men on trans women in Indonesia has left the community feeling anxious and scared. Activists and experts say the violence did not suddenly emerge. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
